text: I absolutely love this app! I tried a few different options before this one and no other timetable/routine app had everything I needed. This app has a free option as well as a small one-time payment option that unlocks all of the features. I paid for the full version and don't regret it for a second. This is sooo helpful for keeping myself on task with my ADHD and the ability to edit routines makes it easy to adjust day to day. The widget option for Android devices is amazing as well! There are so many options for block events and routines, from how they are notified to the color they are on my schedule. I personally like that the notes show up in full on the schedule no matter how long they are so that I can list all the steps of my morning/night routine and don't forget anything. The only thing I wish is that there could be an option to connect this to my computer and have some way to back up my routines/schedule automatically to the cloud. Also, I'd like the ability to make a to do list for each day for things that aren't time-specific, like paying off my credit card and stuff. Like reminders on google calendar, but less annoying, ya know? If there is a way to do this and I'm just missing it, please let me know!

text: I use the app as a kind of whiteboard to create a time plan. I am project oriented so when I have an important event to attend to, I might have to plan my day carefully. (If you're moving, you might not be aware of how much time it takes to do everything until you realize you're running out of time.) To use a personal example, I needed to go to court; I needed to be there at 8am, but I get off work at 11pm the night before. So, as soon as I get off work, I have 8 hours to sleep, but I would have one hour to do everything else. Would 6 hours of sleep free up enough time, or would I have to wake up earlier? I needed to figure out how much time to allocate to sleep, breakfast, getting dressed, going over my case one last time, commuting to a parking lot, walking from the lot to the courthouse, going through security, and waiting at the courtroom by 7:30am. The difference between this app and other planners/calendars is that it asks you how you want to allocate freed up time after you shorten a task. On other apps, you might have to manually adjust every task to close any gaps. Thanks to this app, I realized that I needed to prepare by 8pm the night before, so I was able to ask my boss for a half-day of work instead of working my full hours and rushing the next day.

text:
I love this app. It very easy to use, and it has a visually appealing 
widget. I rate this app only 4 stars for two reasons. The first is that 
setting times for different activities is a little cumbersome. For example, 
if you make a routine, but then find out that you need to wake up an hour 
earlier, you have to go through every single activity and change the start 
and end time. The list of activities also doesn't give a very good visual 
representation of how long each activity is. I would really love to see a 
timeline for a routine, where you could drag and drop the different 
activities on a 24 hour timeline and edit the lengths by dragging the 
edges. I understand that they might be wanting to steer clear from that 
because so many other apps have that function, but I think it's something 
that is is extremely useful and should be considered. The second reason is 
that I can't name the activities! You can only tag them and add a comment, 
so if I want to see exactly what activity I will be doing in the widget or 
on the timeline I am forced to make a separate tag for every single 
activity in order to "name" the activity. If TimeTune added just this one 
feature I would rate it 5 stars.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Thank you very much for your feedback and suggestions, Trevor. The project is still evolving, so some things might change in future versions.

text:
This app is a great start. I think what would make it 5 stars would be the 
following features: 1. import export CSV, 2. drag-and-drop activities 
visually like a Gantt chart, so it is easier to rearrange items and events. 
For example, if I want to move up multiple events by half an hour or push 
events back, I have to edit each item after the change one by one. This is 
not a huge deal once you have perfected your routine, but it would greatly 
help the creation and tweaking of the routine.  3. tracking your time/event 
completion and how closely you follow your routine. You could track them 
with either the amount of time spent or a check box. Some items you just 
need to put in the time, such as practicing an instrument, and some items 
you just need to do and don't require a set amount of time, such as eating 
lunch. I think with those features this app would easily be worth the pro 
purchase. For now, it is helpful for planning a general outline of your 
daily routine, but if you want to hold yourself accountable you need other 
apps. The accountability is really what is needed to ensure you follow your 
routine. I can see this app being potentially a one-stop-shop to help you 
meet your goals and follow your dreams in life, but it is not quite there 
yet. As I said above, it is a really great start and a few more features 
would make it pretty much perfect. P.S.The cloning of activities and 
routines to other days is awesome, and it makes setting up your first 
weekly routine a breeze.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hi Trev! Thank you very much for your suggestions. You're right, the project is still growing and some of these ideas are already on our to-do list. Stay tuned for improvements ;)

text:
I have only been setting up routines, tags, and man. The customization is 
CRAZY good (flexible, make your own thing and it shall fit you) . Type in 
your own tags, choose your tag color out of 20(?not sure) colors and choose 
over 100(again,not sure) logos. You can set up and activate your normal 
routine, and simply toggle a button to change into your holiday routine 
when December starts. Are your Mondays repeated 5 times until Friday? Fear 
not, you can clone activities in a day into other days, and even import 
activities from days in other routines. As far as I can tell, routines are 
not only weekly either , you can set the amount of days a routine has. Be 
warned though, if you are like me and like to explore every single bit of 
settings an app has to offer, you'll spend 3 hours the first time setting 
up the app. After that, you only need to strictly stick to it, and observe 
how good the routine is. If your work piles up, you need to work more. If 
you feel tired, divide your internet or gaming breaks into smaller parts in 
between your work instead of big chunks. There's also a routine statistics, 
showing in percentages how much of a tag (example: sleep) you do in a week. 
And you can see a day's summary, how many hours+minutes do you do each tag, 
starting from the one that takes the most time. It's GREAT. Suggestions for 
the developers though, which I will suggest via the app (yes that is an 
option) : In Routine Statistics, I would love to be able to filter out my 
sleep percentages and only get percentages of other activities that add up 
to 100% (Percentages of waking moments, if you will). That will be a very 
fine addition.

I spent 15 minutes setting up a schedule and was frustrated to find that I had erased my entire afternoon schedule because I made a mistake when changing the end time of something mid-day. This app was, for me, ironically, a waste of time.

developer_reply: Thanks for the feedback, Joshua. 'Until next activity' is there to avoid having to calculate the time yourself, but you can change it after that. Activities don't work like to-do's, they work like chunks of time. If a chunk of time overlaps another one, it'll get overwritten, but the app warns you with a message. That said, we are still improving.

text: This is the ideal app for me. It helps prevent my procrastination and I also use it to help form positive habits. It generally takes 28 days to form a habit, so by creating routines, I find myself more likely to follow through, rather than a to do list that allows me to continue to postponing tasks I dread.   In particular, I'm trying to implement the FLYLady method of keeping my house clean and organized. Setting up a routine makes it so much easier to focus on completion of the tasks, rather then spending more time setting up daily reminders for each task. I like to combine with the Pomodoro method, which is really done by finding a simple Pomodoro timer that suits you in the app store. I accomplish so much more by using this app. I have been using it on and off for a few years but with the new improvements I can't imagine not having this as my main to do and scheduling app. I still have about 9 months left on my premium Todoist account (which is easily integrated) but Time Tune is my go to. It keeps me on track.   I have only two requests that would really thrill me (and perhaps it's available and I just haven't located the ability to do it): I would be so grateful for a Windows version of this that I can sync with my phone. It's so much easier to setup a routine using a "real" keyboard. Also, perhaps we (the users) could exchange and share routines we have setup, using the forums perhaps? For example, housekeeping, children chores, job hunting, etc.   Overall this is one of the most useful apps I have. Thank you so much! I highly recommend to anyone. The initial setup is not as daunting as it might appear and the payoff is well worth it. Highly recommended!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hi Michelle! Thank you very much for your feedback and suggestions. We will analyze the proposed ideas. Meanwhile, have a great day and enjoy your time! ;)

text: This scheduler is severely lacking basic and simple features.  The reminder function needs to give the user the option to select specific and multiple days of the week and dates he or she wants the reminder to repeat itself. The reminder function needs to be able to repeat itself multiple times in a day. When certain events are coming up, I want to be reminded 24 hours, 1 hour, and 5 minutes before to the event.  The reminder function also needs an option to decide the duration of the sound and vibration. I'm sometimes not close to to my phone, and might miss the reminder when it only rings for a few seconds, or even a few minutes. And make it so that you can also set the time with the keypad, not only by turning the clock arms around.

text: The interface is beautifully simple, yet attractive. The ability to switch seamlessly between multiple routines without having to specify date is brilliant. However, ALL other apps I've ever seen use tags to group related activities together. With most apps, if I want to add taking medication to a routine, I'd create the tag Health as an umbrella term to cover all health related activities (doctors appointments, diet, etc.), then add the activity Take Medication. Simple. With TimeTune, I have to either create a tag named Take Medication (along with separate tags for every other activity), or specify each Health related activity in the comments, which can't be seen from the activity list. You only see the name of the tag, making viewing your schedule at a glance confusing when you have multiple activities under one tag. I don't know anything about the programming that goes into making apps, but hopefully this doesn't take all that much effort to fix. Simply being able to give an activity a name, separate from the tag, would make this app SO much more useful.

developer_reply: Hi Laura. Remember that since several versions ago, comments from activities are visible in the schedule and the widget (there are settings to control this at 'Settings / Interface / Behavior' and 'Settings / Widget / Detail'). So basically you can see the schedule as you see it in other apps, the difference is we show the tag before the comment.
